memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "All the tent pegs of the tabernacle and of the surrounding courtyard were bronze." - Exod 38:20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
One verse for the tent pegs. Small pieces of bronze driven into desert ground, holding ropes taut so that everything above stayed upright.

Nobody looked at them. Nobody admired them. They sat in the dirt.

But in a desert with strong winds, the pegs were the difference between a standing tabernacle and a collapsed heap of expensive fabric.

There are people whose whole ministry is peg work. The ones who arrive early and leave late. The ones who pray for others without ever being asked. The grandmother who has interceded for a family for forty years. The person who quietly gives so a ministry can continue.

Isaiah uses this image of a person: God says He will drive him like a peg into a firm place, and he will become a seat of honour for his family (Isa 22:23). Being a peg is not a lesser calling.

And Jesus said that whoever wants to be great must be a servant (Matt 20:26-27). Greatness in God's kingdom is measured from the ground up.

If nobody sees what you do, you are in good company. God notices what holds things up.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you willing to do work that nobody notices?
2. Who are the "pegs" in your church or family?
3. Does the desire to be seen affect where you are willing to serve?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, make me content to be a peg in the ground if that is where You want me. Amen.
